answer: Convex admission fees demand 1,000 units for entry, scaling quadratically to penalize volume. An honest user secures a crystal shard at the entry knoll for 1,000, while a farm seeking 1,000 identities must expend 1,000,000,000 units to harbor them. Verifiers audit the registry for crystal usage at each knoll, rejecting any duplicate harbor. Without refunds, identity expansion is prohibitively costly for fakes.
